slot.brief: Magnetic flux varies with time as a polynomial/sinusoid; differentiate the flux expression and evaluate the induced emf at a specified instant.

stem: A closed coil of resistance $0.20\ \text{\Omega}$ has flux linkage $\lambda(t)=(0.10t^3+0.20t)\ \text{Wb-turn}$, where $t$ is in seconds. What is the magnitude of the induced current at $t=2.0\ \text{s}$?
working:
$|\mathcal E|=\left|\dfrac{d\lambda}{dt}\right|=|0.30t^2+0.20|$

Independent check: Induced emf magnitude: $|d\lambda/dt|=0.30t^2+0.20=1.4\,\text{V}$ at $t=2.0\,\text{s}$. Thus $I=1.4/0.20=7.0\,\text{A}$.
solution:
By Faraday’s law, $|\mathcal E|=|d\lambda/dt|=|0.30t^2+0.20|$.
At $t=2.0\,\text{s}$, $|\mathcal E|=1.4\,\text{V}$, so
$$I=\frac{|\mathcal E|}{R}=\frac{1.4}{0.20}=7.0\,\text{A}.$$
